chunks: 5. Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Kufi narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, who said: Ali ibn al-Abbas narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Asbat narrated from Sayf ibn 'Umairah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
regarding His Mighty and Exalted Word: (And I breathed into him of My Spirit). He (peace be upon him) said: From My power.
ai.seo_question: What does 'My Spirit' mean in the context of God breathing into Adam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that the 'spirit' (ruh) breathed into Adam is not a distinct created entity but rather a metaphor for God’s power (qudra). This interpretation aligns with the Shia theological emphasis on divine simplicity, rejecting the idea of a separate, substantial soul infused into humans while affirming God’s direct creative act.
